From 64bd9c8135751b561f27edaaffe93d07093f81af Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Florian Fainelli <f.fainelli@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Oct 2018 15:06:33 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] net: bcmgenet: Poll internal PHY for GENETv5

On GENETv5, there is a hardware issue which prevents the GENET hardware
from generating a link UP interrupt when the link is operating at
10Mbits/sec. Since we do not have any way to configure the link
detection logic, fallback to polling in that case.

Fixes: 421380856d9c ("net: bcmgenet: add support for the GENETv5 hardware")
Signed-off-by: Florian Fainelli <f.fainelli@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/broadcom/genet/bcmmii.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/broadcom/genet/bcmmii.c
index 4241ae928d4a..34af5f1569c8 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/broadcom/genet/bcmmii.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/broadcom/genet/bcmmii.c
@@ -321,9 +321,12 @@ int bcmgenet_mii_probe(struct net_device *dev)
 	phydev->advertising = phydev->supported;
 
 	/* The internal PHY has its link interrupts routed to the
-	 * Ethernet MAC ISRs
+	 * Ethernet MAC ISRs. On GENETv5 there is a hardware issue
+	 * that prevents the signaling of link UP interrupts when
+	 * the link operates at 10Mbps, so fallback to polling for
+	 * those versions of GENET.
 	 */
-	if (priv->internal_phy)
+	if (priv->internal_phy && !GENET_IS_V5(priv))
 		dev->phydev->irq = PHY_IGNORE_INTERRUPT;
 
 	return 0;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/net/ethernet/broadcom/genet/bcmmii.c`**
   - Added a comment explaining a hardware issue with GENETv5 that prevents link UP interrupts from being generated when operating at 10Mbps.
   - Modified the conditional check for setting `dev->phydev->irq` to ignore interrupts. The check now includes a condition to ensure that this only applies if the device is not a GENETv5 (`!GENET_IS_V5(priv)`).

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in `bcmmii.c` are directly related to addressing a specific hardware limitation of the GENETv5. The added comment provides context for the change, indicating that the fallback to polling is necessary due to the inability of the hardware to signal link status correctly at lower speeds. The conditional logic change ensures that the interrupt handling is appropriately adjusted for GENETv5 devices, thereby preventing potential issues with link detection in this specific scenario.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (priv->internal_phy)
    dev->phydev->irq = PHY_IGNORE_INTERRUPT;
```
Reason:
The code checks if the internal PHY is present and, if so, it ignores link interrupts by setting the interrupt request (irq) to `PHY_IGNORE_INTERRUPT`. This is problematic on GENETv5 hardware because it cannot generate a link UP interrupt when operating at 10Mbps, leading to a reliance on interrupts that do not occur, thus failing to detect link status changes.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (priv->internal_phy && !GENET_IS_V5(priv))
    dev->phydev->irq = PHY_IGNORE_INTERRUPT;
```
Reason:
The patch adds a condition to check if the hardware is not GENETv5 (`!GENET_IS_V5(priv)`) before ignoring the link interrupts. This ensures that for GENETv5, the system will not ignore interrupts, allowing for a fallback to polling for link status updates, which is necessary due to the hardware limitation at 10Mbps.
